name: MAIN STREET, DAWN
materialIdentity: Room 2's street at first light, in tune: the false fronts warm in the low sun from the east, the windows dark, the sky clearing from gold to blue, the dog on his back in the road (doc 48 S7, errata 99 J)
note: Room 36, doc 20: Main Street at dawn, which replaces Room 2 after F5. Doc 48 S7: not a cutscene -- the player walks the street they know, reads the nine dawn hotspots, and the game ends at the one exit, the coach stop east: Thad's last line, then the Act IV letter over black. Its pixels are Room 2's under the morning's light (tools/art/room36-dawn.py).

exits.name: THE COACH STOP

LOOK_AT.say: The road out to the coach stop, the same way I came in, the other way round.
repeat: First light on the ruts. At this hour they look almost deliberate.
Somewhere down there is the sign at the edge of town, and whatever number it says this morning.

LISTEN_TO.say: The road, quiet, the way roads are before anybody has had an opinion about them.
repeat: Wind coming down the road from the hills, cold, and in no hurry.
Somewhere behind me a shutter going up. The town is starting again.

then.speaker: thad
then.line: I was robbed, and it was the making of me.

then.speaker: thad
then.line: The gold is real. The story is better. I will tell you both in the spring.

transitScene.sceneLine: docs/48-act-turn-beats.md::## S7 · MAIN STREET, DAWN (the close) · beat 3

exits.note: Doc 48 S7: 'The one exit is the coach stop, east.' Beat 3 at the coach stop (coach_stop_dawn, errata 121 B): Thad's last spoken line, then beat 4, the Act IV letter over black (doc 04 Part Three's, as Room 19 reads it). No document writes the stop a LOOK or LISTEN: a stub (errata 72 F). Beat 5's credits are not built (doc 36 Q176). Errata 189: its LOOK and LISTEN are doc 106's (linesFrom), and it is no longer a stub.

generated.note: GENERATED. Edit the documents or the annotation, never this file.

entrances.note: As Room 2: the street's east edge, facing down it.
Out of the filing (F5), onto the street at first light.

LOOK_AT.say: Under all the claims and disputes, one new notice, official, sealed, correctly spelled. It has the whole board's attention.
repeat: Claims for sale, claims disputed, and a new one: CLAIM ONE, FILED, O. MOTT, WORKINGS TO COMMENCE. The lost dog notice has been taken down.
Somebody has drawn a small raccoon in the corner of the official notice. I'm choosing not to know who.

LISTEN_TO.say: Paper in wind. This morning it sounds like applause. I'm aware that's me.
repeat: Paper, in wind. Less of it.
One sheet has come loose and gone off down the street, taking its business elsewhere.

LOOK_AT.say: The dog, in the early sun, in the middle of the street, on his back.
repeat: Bill. He is sitting with somebody now. He does not appear to have noticed a difference.
He has rolled over to warm the other side. He had the right idea all along.
then: He has always known something the rest of us are only learning this morning.

LISTEN_TO.say: Breathing. Contented. The town's oldest solvency, undiluted.
repeat: Breathing. Contented. He remains the only solvent resident of Consolation.
A small snore. The most honest sound on Main Street, and this morning it has competition.

overrides.TALK_TO: I thanked him. For nothing in particular. For being the town's one solvent institution. He accepted on the street's behalf.

LOOK_AT.say: The tallest thing in Consolation, catching the first light, as is its habit and its right.
repeat: The tallest thing in Consolation, and the only building as deep as it is tall.
A bird has landed on the cross at the top. It is the only thing in town higher than the bell, and it is not making anything of it.

LISTEN_TO.say: The bell. In tune. Sowerby has not changed how he strikes it.
repeat: The bell again, the note settling into the hills. It took this town twelve years to sound like this.
The last of the bell, fading. Under it, nothing out of tune at all.
then: Nothing changed but everything under it.

LOOK_AT.say: The gilt is peeling off the lettering in the morning sun.
repeat: The C in COMPANY has already gone. It reads IMPROVEMENT OMPANY, which is more accurate than it used to be.
Nobody is standing under it. For twelve years somebody was always standing under it, waiting to be let in.
then: Nobody will repaint it now, and the sign has the good grace to know it.

LISTEN_TO.say: It creaks. It would like to be taken down. I know another sign that felt that way.
repeat: The creak again. It has said its piece and keeps on saying it.
The chain ticking against the bracket. It will come down in its own time.

LOOK_AT.say: Three inches of water, and this morning, the whole sky in it.
repeat: Somebody has cleaned it. It is still three inches of water, and it is clean water.
I can see my own face in it, and the sky behind, and neither of us looks worried.

LISTEN_TO.say: The thing that lives in it, surfacing. We have both made it through.
repeat: A small ripple. It has decided I am not a threat.
Nothing for a moment, then a bubble. We are both still here.

LOOK_AT.say: Six inches above the mud, same as ever. The distinction matters less this morning.
repeat: Somebody has swept it. Not the street: just the boardwalk, end to end, at dawn, for no reason anyone will admit to.
I stood on the loose board on purpose. It said what it always says. I find I had missed it.
then: Everyone is walking in the middle of the street anyway.

LISTEN_TO.say: The loose board, third from the end. Still loose. Somebody should see to that.
repeat: Boots further down, slow ones. Nobody is in a hurry this morning.
The loose board, under my own weight this time. A friendly note. A little flat.

LOOK_AT.say: The hills, gone gold at the top — the ordinary kind, the kind the sun hands out free every morning and nobody ever had to dig for.
repeat: Gold country. For the first time since I arrived, that is simply a true statement.
The diggings are quiet, and the hills look, for once, like hills.

LISTEN_TO.say: Very faint, and for the first time since I stepped off the coach: no picks.
repeat: Nothing. They are extremely large, and they are not doing anything, and there is gold in them.
The wind coming down off them, cool, carrying nothing at all. It is a relief to hear nothing in a place that used to be so loud about it.

overrides.TALK_TO: I told them they could rest now. Presumptuous, possibly. But somebody ought to say it, and the piano man had the morning free.

LOOK_AT.say: The same mud. It held my boot the first night and the truth the whole time.
repeat: The same mud. I know it now.
My boot print from the first night is long gone. The mud kept the truth and let the rest go.
then: The only honest thing in the territory, as I believe I remarked.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. It never once lied to me. Even now it declines to start.
repeat: Nothing. It never had anything to say and it never pretended otherwise, and in this town that made it remarkable.
A drip off the boardwalk into it, slow, unbothered, in no hurry for anything.

overrides.PICK_UP: I took a little, in a twist of paper. The one honest thing in the territory. A man should keep a sample of what saved him.

LOOK_AT.say: The same two-story faces on the same one-story buildings — but at dawn, with the light behind them, they look like what they always were: a promise somebody kept badly and everybody kept anyway.
repeat: Two stories tall in front and one story deep. It is still a stage set. It is just that people live here.
A man is painting one of them. Not the front: the back, where nobody will see it.

LISTEN_TO.say: Wind behind them, same as ever. It sounds less empty than it did. That may be me.
repeat: Wind. There is still a great deal of nothing behind these. It has stopped being funny and started being a fact about somebody's home.
Somebody behind one of them, frying something. The fronts finally have something behind them worth the name.

props.note: Errata 187. Tyler, 2026-11-08: "At dawn I think the horses should all be gone. Just the hitching post is there." Room 2's hitching rail, empty: cut from the night group's rest frame, at the engine's own scale for it, graded as the night draws it and then under the dawn's light (tools/art/hitching-rail-dawn.py). Its obstacle stays. Errata 198 moved the night group back to 1405,755, and the empty rail with it, re-cut at the scale the room's curve gives there. Errata 201 moved the night group right to 1470 and drew it at a horse's true size, its hooves on 746; the empty rail follows, re-cut at the new scale (385 x 227), its base line on 755, the foot of the night frame below the hooves.

figureLight.note: Errata 265 (Tyler, 2026-11-10: "Fix the dawn"). Errata 263 relit this street to the very first light (mean 98.6 to 63.9) and left the two figures on it as bright as the old morning: the dog was an orange lamp on a dim street. A cold light, dimmer, and a little of their colour out, so they stand in the dawn the street is in.

motion.note: Errata 273: the room's own small motion (engine/render/MotionLayer.ts). Placed by eye on the plate; nothing here waits on a puzzle's flag.

occluders.note: Errata 302 (Tyler, 2026-11-13: "make sure Thad isn't walking in front of posts on the porch when he should be walking behind them"). Every porch post on the street, read off the plate at 3x: its column from the roof beam to its foot, and the row its foot stands on. A man whose feet are above that row is behind the post and it is cut out of him; at or below it he is in front. The Nugget's posts stand twenty pixels back from the deck's edge and the hotel's at three depths, which is why it is per post and not per box. The Company's and the assay office's columns are pilasters on their walls, and nobody stands behind those. The hotel's two left-hand posts stand at the back of its deck, behind anyone who can stand on it, and are not listed.
